slides.title: Onsoo Botanicals in the US
Key questions

claims.claim: Should Onsoo enter the US in 2027, and by which route, to build toward $40M of US revenue by 2030 within the board's cash, payback and margin limits?
evidence: Success criteria: Cumulative US cash need of no more than $18M through 2030; US cash flow back to zero by the end of 2030; Group operating margin at or above 8% in every year; On the way to $40M of US revenue by 2030; Only one major new-market launch in 2027
Decision maker: CEO Park Ji-won and the board
Timing: Board meeting, March 2027
Out of scope: Makeup and hair care; DTC-led and mass-retail-led routes (not modeled); Markets other than the US and Japan; Price changes

evidence: 41% of US K-beauty skincare sales went through Amazon in 2025

evidence: 29% of first-time pilot buyers bought again within 90 days

slides.title: 1c: US repeat purchase is that of a new brand: 29% of pilot buyers came back, against 48% in Korea

Against Korea: US buyers repeat at 60% of the Korean rate, the gap a wider range and a known brand have to close

The Amazon-led route clears the cash cap and margin floor with ease, but its payback depends on ad cost

slides.title: 2d: The plan's 25% ad cost sits below the whole benchmark range, where scaling brands pay a median 32%

evidence: Benchmark range across brands scaling from $5M to $20M a year: 26%–38%

claims.claim: 28% Onsoo's pilot, January–June 2026, achieved on a small budget, already above the plan's 25%
32% median for skincare brands scaling from $5M to $20M a year on Amazon US; Option A's revenue crosses exactly this band in 2027–29; costs per click rise as brands bid on broader keywords
$4.7M less cumulative cash by 2030 at 32% ad cost than at 25%, enough to turn the 2030 payback into a shortfall
evidence: $0.24 a unit for each percentage point, on every planned unit

claims.claim: Plan for 28% and treat anything above it as a signal to slow the ad-funded ramp

slides.title: 2d: A higher US import duty would leave Option A paying back only if ad cost nears the plan's level

claims.claim: 32% (benchmark median) misses payback; low point near −$3.2M
evidence: End-2030 15% duty −$2.3M; 25% duty −$3.4M; low point −$3.2M

claims.claim: 38% (benchmark high) misses widely, still inside the cap
evidence: End-2030 15% duty −$6.4M; 25% duty −$7.5M; low point −$6.4M
every case stays far inside the $18M cap

slides.title: 2e: No modeled route reaches $40M by 2030, and the Amazon route gets two-thirds of the way

66% of the $40M ambition reached by Option A in 2030

normalized.recommendation: Launch on Amazon in 2027 under four gates; add retail only above 20% awareness. Keep ad cost at or below 28%, and lower that ceiling if the duty rises. Reset $40M as a post-2030 goal; Option A reaches $26.4M in 2030. (Option A · Amazon-led: "Recommend, with ad cost held at or below 28%"; Option B: Reject; Option J: Keep for 2028.)

alternatives_considered.treatment: Recommend, with ad cost held at or below 28%: the only route inside the board's limits; cash low point −$1.9M, $26.4M revenue in 2030; pays back at blended ad cost up to 28.6%.

Reject: breaks the cap, the payback and the margin floor; −$20.8M cumulative cash at end-2030 on its own inputs, about $26M when corrected for the halo and for 2.6 units per door per week; group margin 4.5% in 2027.
Keep for 2028: more cash to 2030 ($1.8M), but small ($7M added revenue in 2030) and outside the US; the one-launch limit applies only to 2027.
Not modeled by the planning team; DTC and mass retail carry 12% and 14% of K-beauty sales. Out of scope.
Raised to 20%: at 10–20% awareness the median newcomer sells 3.5 units, under the 4.0 line, so a 15% awareness trigger is too low.
Replaced by a ceiling at the pilot's 28%, reviewed quarterly; 25% sits below the whole benchmark range where scaling brands pay a median 32%.

alternatives_considered.option: Adding makeup and hair care (wider categories)
alternatives_considered.treatment: Out of scope: the decision covers Onsoo's skincare range.

assumptions_and_uncertainties: Payback by 2030 holds only while blended ad cost stays at or below 28.6%; scaling brands pay a median 32% (benchmark range 26%–38%)
The plan's 25% ad cost rests on ad cost falling as the brand matures and is below the 26% low end of the benchmark range
The planning team applies the hero product's per-unit economics to all SKUs, which is unproven
The 2027 step-up to 300,000 units (1.8x the pilot's June pace) is plausible, but not yet proven
Whether repeat rises once seven SKUs are listed is untested; the plan needs repeat to hold as SKUs are added
A full year of 2027 sales needs the cross-border listings kept live until Onsoo's own listings take over
US import duty decision expected mid-2027; at 25% duty break-even ad cost falls to 26.9%; a weaker won would offset part of a rise
At 80% of plan volume, end-2030 cash is only $0.1M even at 25% ad cost
The 1.3x Amazon halo in Option B rests on a 0.71 correlation that may run the other way; removed brands such as Mooncrest may be missing from the memo's data
Four peer brands show a pattern, not proof: one of three Amazon-first entrants reached scale, so Option A still has to earn its volume
Option B correction case ignores that at 2.6 units the retailer would remove Onsoo after 12 months
Model leaves out taxes, exchange-rate moves and anything after 2030
No working capital given in the pack for Option J
Synthetic benchmark data: the company and every figure are fictional
